# Conformance data

What the real core rules give for every goal in every week of the demo workspace. A rebuild proves its rules by reading the same workspace and producing the same rows: every row, every column. `src/spec/conformance.test.ts` recomputes them from `workspace.json` with Faro’s own rules and fails on any difference, so these files always say what the code does.

The ports’ contracts are here too, as cases any build runs through a small shim: [the port contracts](contracts/README.md).

## The input: workspace.json

The demo workspace (Platform Engineering, 126 goals, 5249 check-ins, a 53-week goal year starting 2025-12-22), built for 2026-11-05T12:00:00.000Z (week 45), trimmed to the records the core rules read: the cycle, people, teams, goals, check-ins, decisions (what was said in reviews), asks, reviews and watches, and, under `modules`, the records of the modules that add rows here (metrics). Their fields are in [the data model](../core/data-model.md). It is one JSON object; each array holds one record per line. Asks are under `requests` (the stored table’s name).

## How each week is judged

Weeks 0 to the cycle’s week at `builtFor` (`currentWeek(cycle, builtFor)`: 45 here). Week *w* is judged at its review day, noon UTC: the cycle’s start + 7·*w* + `reviewDay` days, at 12:00 (`weekMoment`). That moment is “today” for every rule. The workspace is taken as it stood then (`asOf`):

- goals added by then (`createdAt`), and not stopped by then (`stoppedAt`);
- check-ins posted by then (`postedAt`);
- decisions made by then (`at`);
- asks raised by then (`createdAt`); one answered or done later is open again with no answer (answered and done are both timed by `answeredAt`), and one withdrawn later (`updatedAt`) is open again.

“By then” means at or before the moment (ISO timestamps compared as text). Days without an update count calendar days (UTC).

**Two cuts, both applied.** Every rule reads only the check-ins posted by the moment. The calculation, the projection and the scorecard (the rules’ “check-ins up to week *w*”) then also keep only those with `week` ≤ *w*; the official status, its latest check-in, the flags and the trend take every check-in posted by the moment, whatever week it is for.

**Not self-explanatory:** goals are taken as they are now in every week: their plan history (`planHistory`) says which plan applied when, but other edits (a stage’s due week, a goal linked to an ask later) are not replayed. The rows are made the same way, so a rebuild that reads workspace.json the same way matches them. So every field but `createdAt` and `stoppedAt` (which make the cut above) is read whatever the week: a goal with `stoppedAt` set has no `hit` cell even in the weeks before it was stopped ([the scorecard](../core/rules/scorecard.md)); one with `unmeasuredSince` set is held to no number in every week, before that day too ([a goal held to no number](../core/rules/unmeasured.md)); and `proposedAt` is not read by the cut, so a goal still proposed is in every week’s rows from its `createdAt`, judged like any other (the demo and edge workspaces have none).

**Not self-explanatory:** two different check-ins are “the latest”: the official status (and `latest_week`, `greener`, days without an update) takes the one posted most recently, by `postedAt`; the calculation, projection and scorecard take the last by week, then posting. They differ when a check-in for an earlier week is posted later (a backfill). Ties are broken the same way in both, from a goal’s check-ins sorted by week, then `postedAt`, keeping `workspace.json`’s order where both are equal: the official status walks that list and takes a new latest only on a strictly later `postedAt`, so of two posted at the same moment it keeps the one for the earlier week (the earlier record when the weeks are equal too); the calculation takes the last of the list, so of two for the same week posted at the same moment it takes the later record. (The demo workspace has no such ties; [the edge-case workspace](#the-edge-case-workspace-edge) has both, on E-9 and E-10.)

Rows go by week, then goals in key order (G-1, G-2 … G-126).

What each column is, and the rule that gives it:

- **status.csv** ([the status](../core/rules/status.md)): `status` is the official status, `goalStatus(goal, cycle, checkIns, moment).status`; `calculated` is what the numbers say (`.calc`, from `assessPosted` in the current week); `greener` whether the latest call is greener than its calculation; `latest_week` the week of the latest check-in (by when it was posted), empty with none; `days_without_update` from `daysWithoutUpdate`. Codes as in [the vocabulary](../core/vocabulary.md). With no check-in posted yet, `greener` is `no` and `latest_week` is empty.
- **flags.csv** ([flags](../core/rules/flags.md)): `flags` the flag codes worst first, separated by spaces (empty with none); `handled` what puts it in hand ([being handled](../core/rules/flags.md#being-handled-and-needs-attention)): `action` (an open action with a due week, agreed since its latest check-in) or `answered` (at risk only: a decision ask answered since), else empty. Only those two: marking a goal reviewed or noting it is a look, never in hand (`lookedAtFor`, not a column here), so `noted` and `reviewed` never appear; `needs_attention` `yes` or `no`; `attention_group` the goal’s group on the Needs attention list (`needs`, `handled`) or empty when it isn’t on it.
- **projection.csv** ([the projection](../core/rules/projection.md)): for a number to move, the projection `assessPosted` makes (to its due week, from the check-ins up to this week), and `forecast_misses`; for a number to keep in range, one number per week (the latest posted in each week), projected to the cycle’s end, made whether or not the goal is stale (the scorecard itself says Can’t say when stale); `forecast_misses` always empty. With no projection every column after `kind` is empty, `forecast_misses` included; with one, a number to move has `forecast_misses` `yes` or `no`, from the projected value as the projection gives it, not rounded to the goal’s decimals (74.6 against a target of 75 is `yes`). `slope` is the slope the projection leans by (*lean* × the fitted slope), not the fitted slope. `value`, `low`, `high` and `slope` are rounded to 6 decimal places; `first_week` and `last_week` are the weeks of numbers the line used, `to_week` the week projected to.
- **scorecard.csv** ([the scorecard](../core/rules/scorecard.md)): `goalScorecard(goal, cycle, checkIns, week, stale)` with `stale` when the status is `stale`; one row per cell, in order. `cell`, `tone` and `likelihood` are the rule, and all this file holds: a rebuild in other words, or in another language, still scores. `likelihood` is the code (`likely`, `possible`, `unlikely`, `very-unlikely`) on a `hit` cell that has a likelihood, and empty on every other cell and on a `hit` cell that says Can’t say or Too early to say.
- **scorecard-words.csv** (scored when asked, `"also": ["scorecard-words"]`): the same rows, keyed the same way, with the words each cell says: `value`, `label` and `sub` ([every one of them](../core/rules/scorecard.md#the-words)).
- **checkin.csv** ([what a check-in must say](../core/rules/check-in.md)): one row per check-in in `workspace.json` (`checkin` is its `id`), judged again as a draft by `evaluate` in its own `week`, for the goal with the plan of that week (`goalAsOf`), with every check-in in the workspace (the rule uses those for earlier weeks), **not** cut by posting time: an earlier week’s check-in posted after this one (a backfill, a correction) still counts as an earlier check-in here, unlike `moment` below. First the **bare draft**: the check-in’s number (written as the stored number, `String(value)`; empty when null) or its stage updates, and nothing else, the owner’s call left to the calculation: `calculated` (`on`, `risk`, `off` or `done`: `planned` and `none` count as `on`), `reason` (`ahead`, `behind` or empty), `asks_target` and `needs_path` (`yes`/`no`), `missing` (the codes still missing, in order, separated by spaces; empty when it can be posted). Then the same bare draft with only the owner’s call as posted added (`call`, the check-in’s `status`; the posted words, cause, path and target are not attached): `greener` and `call_missing`. Last, `moment`, [the habit](../core/rules/habit.md)’s rule 3 for the check-in as posted, against the goal’s check-ins posted before it (`postedAt` earlier): `reached`, `back {k}` (back on track; *k* is this week minus the first week of the unbroken run of behind calls before it, a week with no check-in not breaking the run, so it can be more than the number of check-ins) or empty. “The week before” there is the latest earlier week that has a check-in posted before this one, not necessarily week − 1. Rows go by week, then goal key, then id.

- **find.csv** ([finding things](../core/rules/finding.md)): stage 3’s (`"stage": 3` in `drill.json`), not part of stage 1, where it is scored only when asked (`"also": ["find"]` in `drill.json`, or `--files find`). One row per search in `screen-cases.json`’s `find`, in its order (the find rules’ worked examples), made on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (the same `asOf`; people have no job title in workspace.json, so a person is found by name and team only): `kind` (`goal`, `person` or `team`) and `q` the search; `total` how many match (when nothing matched and a near miss did, how many match the near miss: the rows shown); `near` the near miss offered when nothing matched, else empty; `ids` the ids of every row found (the near miss’s when there is one), in the kind’s order, separated by spaces. Goals are the live goals not stopped by then, worst first then by title; people are those not marked as left, those whose name starts with the search first, then A to Z; teams A to Z. A goal is found by its title, key, owner, team, level, status word, its latest check-in’s reason (`why`), path to green (`pathToGreen.what`) and what it needs (`pathToGreen.needs`), its definition, its source and its unit (`goalWords`, [finding things](../core/rules/finding.md)).

- **page-header.csv** ([one page header](../core/rules/page-header.md)): stage 3’s, for every address navigation.csv answers: its kind of page (`pageKind`: list, detail or task), its name, and what the phone’s top bar says with the title in view and once it has gone (`topBarSays`; “the workspace” stands for the workspace’s name, and a task has no top bar).
- **goal-row.csv** ([one goal row](../core/rules/goal-row.md)): not part of stage 1. What `rowParts` gives for every live goal in six places (`goals-list`, `watching-needs`, `watching-handled`, `checkin-queue` with no draft, `agenda`, `home-mine`), as `amara`, on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor`. `value`, `gap`, `as_of` and `result` are the value slot; `reason` and `context` the sentences, each with `1` in `reason_flag` or `context_flag` when it takes the warning mark; `action` the one button, empty when the place has none.
- **form-footer.csv** ([one form footer](../core/rules/form-footer.md)): not part of stage 1. The words a form’s footer and its one exit say, from `src/domain/formFooter.ts`: `case` is the kind (`close` the exit, `next` a step’s primary, `primary` a last step’s, `status` the line above the buttons, `fix` the error summary, `draft` a resumed draft’s step line, `primary-ok` whether a label may stand alone), `given` the situation, `says` the words exactly. A draft’s day is worked out from 18 Nov 2026 at noon, local time.
- **goals.csv** ([the query port](../rebuild/ports-at-scale.md#the-query-port-what-screens-and-the-ai-tools-read)): not part of stage 1, scored like find.csv when asked (`"also": ["goals"]`). What the query port’s `goals()` and `counts()` give for each query in a fixed list, on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor`. `query` is the query as a Goals link’s parameters (empty for every goal: worst first, then by title); `total` how many live goals (not stopped) match; `near` the near miss tried when a search found nothing, else empty; then `counts()`: how many of them in each status (`off` to `done`), and `attention` how many need attention under the same query with its attention filter left off (the Goals switch’s count: being handled doesn’t count); `ids` every goal found, in order across all its pages, separated by spaces. `checkedin=no` keeps the goals due this week with no check-in yet, and `checkedin=asked` those checked in by the due day after an ask for an update, by [the habit](../core/rules/habit.md)’s standing (rule 1); `inreview=<id>` keeps the goals that review walks, and none for a review that isn’t there. The contract `goalsContract` (`src/ports/contracts/goals.ts`) runs these rows against any adapter, with its four checks: the rows’ status and flags are those in status.csv and flags.csv for that week; keyset paging gives every goal once while goals are added between pages; no page is larger than 50; only `goal()` gives a goal’s check-ins.

- **navigation.csv** ([navigation](../core/rules/navigation.md)): stage 3’s, scored like find.csv (`"also": ["navigation"]`). For two viewers (`rhea`, who owns goals; `oskar`, who owns none: `owns_goals`) at each address in `screen-cases.json`’s `navigation`: `menu` the sidebar’s items in order, its groups (your work, look up, make, this workspace and you) separated by ` | `, and `tabs` the phone’s four (More holds the rest), as ids separated by spaces; `owns_goals` is whether they have a goal to check in on (one of theirs, not stopped or done); `lit` the menu item lit there, or empty (also when the item that would light isn’t in this viewer’s menu: Oskar, who owns no goal, has no Check-in item, so nothing lights at `/check-in`); `page` the page’s name in the top bar and the browser’s title (rule 2: a goal, review, person or team by its own name from the workspace; Help’s articles aren’t in the workspace, so an article’s page is named “Help”). The addresses with `example` are a module’s item and pages (named “Example”); everywhere else no module adds an item. The last six rows are Home in a workspace with features switched off (Workspace → Features), three for each viewer, the address marked so: `/ (Reviews off)`, Reviews off (no `reviews` in the menu, and the phone’s tabs without it); `/ (Feedback off)`, Feedback off (no `feedback`: the last group is `workspace settings help`); and `/ (every feature off)`, every optional feature off (neither). Nothing else on these rows changes: the lit item is `home` and the page is “Home”.

- **import.csv** ([kinds, levels and near misses](../core/rules/import-levels.md)): stage 2’s, with changes.csv, and the spreadsheets stage’s; scored like find.csv (`"also": ["import"]` from another stage). One row per case: a set of rows loaded through the change engine on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (week 45), by `actor` (amara is an admin; tunde is not), into `sheet` (`goals`, `checkIns` or `people`). `rows` is the rows as JSON, column name to cell, numbered from row 2 in order; `answers` the answers given, as JSON, group id to choice (empty for none); `given`, what the case starts from beyond the workspace, as JSON (empty for nothing): `mode` `create` for set-up from nothing (every row new), `stopped`, goals by key stopped before it (in the archive, as a whole-cycle export carries them), and `sheets`, other sheets’ rows loaded in the same file. People in workspace.json have no email, so their email is empty and rows name them by name or ID. Every case is loaded through the spreadsheet door (`via` `spreadsheet`), set-up’s `create` mode too, so every item’s Via is `Spreadsheet`. `rows`, `answers` and `given` are written back as compact JSON (`JSON.stringify` of the case’s own objects, keys in the case’s order, no spaces). Then what the engine says: `kind`, `level` (`must` or `check`), `group` (its group id) and `message` (its sentence) of the first problem or question in the file’s order (sheet, then row; a note is neither), empty when there is none; `must` and `questions` how many Must-fix groups and Check groups; `saves` `yes` when it would save: no Must fix, no open question, no reason missing and at least one item (a file that changes nothing, every row left alone, says `no`), and never in set-up from a file (`given.mode` `create`), which commits nothing and says `no` with all four true; `kinds`, every kind it raised, notes too, each once, in the order first raised, separated by spaces. Every kind the engine raises has a case ([the issue kinds](../core/import-issues.md)).

- **changes.csv** ([the change engine](../core/rules/change-engine.md)): stage 2’s, with import.csv (`"stage": 2` in `drill.json`). The same cases as import.csv, run the same way, and more that save (`saves-check-in`, `saves-plan-with-reason`, `saves-new-goal`, `saves-person`, `saves-stop`, `saves-tree-by-ref`, and `corrects-keeps-author`: an admin’s row replacing this week’s check-in on a goal someone else owns, with `given.reason`, the import’s reason box). Rows are matched by `case` and `row`. Row 0 is the case: `actor`, `sheet`, `rows`, `answers` and `given` as in import.csv; `counts`, every count of the change set that isn’t 0 as `key=n` separated by spaces, in this order: `newGoals`, `goals`, `plans`, `checkIns` (every check-in, those that replace one too), `backfilled` (check-ins for an earlier week, a replacing one too, so it counts in both), `replaced` (check-ins that replace one already there), `people`, `newPeople`, `teams`, `stopped`, `deleted`, `left` (a row that changes a goal’s plan counts in `plans`, not `goals`, whatever else it changes: a Target and a Definition together is `plans` 1, `goals` 0); `unchanged`, the rows that change nothing; `needs_reason`, `yes` when a plan change, or a check-in corrected, needs a reason none was given; and `saves`, `yes` when the change set would save (never in set-up from a file, `given.mode` `create`, which commits nothing). Rows 1 on are its items, in the engine’s order (a sheet’s rows in order, then what they lead to): `sheet` (Goals, Plan, Check-ins or People) and `line` (the row in that sheet, from 2), `target` (the goal’s ID, a new one being `goal_c1` and on in the order the engine asks for IDs; empty for a person or team), `name` (the goal’s, person’s or team’s name), `kind` (`new goal`, `goal`, `plan`, `check-in`, `replaces check-in`, `person`, `new person`, `team`, `stop goal`, `delete goal` or `person left`), `diffs` (every field it changes as `Field: before → after`, the field’s label and values in the words a person reads, `—` for nothing, joined by ` | `), `needs_reason` (`yes` for a plan change after check-ins started, or a correction without a reason), and `author` (a check-in’s: the id of the person it belongs to once saved, `rhea`, not their name; replacing one keeps who checked in, Lane, 14 Nov; empty on row 0 and for other kinds). A case that blocks still lists the items it would make.

- **change-cases.json** (stage 2): the cases import.csv and changes.csv run, input only, in order: `[{ case, actor, sheet, rows, answers?, given? }]`, with `rows` and `given` as objects, not JSON in a cell. The harness puts a copy beside the `workspace.json` it hands a stage 2 command, so a rebuild reads its cases from there; in the CSV files those columns are the same inputs written back.
- **screen-cases.json** (stage 3): the cases navigation.csv, find.csv, readback.csv and home.csv run, input only (`ScreenCases` in `src/spec/conformance.ts`): `workspaceName`, the name the screens say; `navigation`, its `viewers`, the core’s `addresses`, a module’s menu item (`module`: `id`, `to`, `label`, `group`) and the `moduleAddresses` answered with it in the menu, and `switchedOff`, Home with features off (`address`, the marked address the row carries, and `off`, the module ids switched off, or `all`); `find`, each search as `{ kind, q }` in order; `readback`, a `blank` goal (every field of New goal’s draft as the form starts it) and the `cases`, each `{ case, viewer, draft }` with `draft` the fields set over the blank goal; `home`, its `viewers` and `days` (each an ISO time, noon UTC). The harness puts a copy beside the `workspace.json` it hands a command, as it does change-cases.json, so a rebuild reads its cases from there and never from the expected files.
- **readback.csv** ([the read-back](../core/rules/read-back.md)): stage 3’s, scored like find.csv (`"also": ["readback"]` from another stage). One row per case in `screen-cases.json`’s `readback`: a draft goal (`draft`, the fields set over its `blank` goal, as JSON: numbers and weeks as text, as typed, weeks counted from the cycle’s start, a stage’s due week as `stages[].dueWeek`, `alsoHelps` as goal ids) on New goal’s last step, seen by `viewer`, on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (Thursday 5 Nov 2026, week 45, the review day), with the weekly rhythm and Reviews on, each question it raises taken as answered, the level as New goal starts it when the draft doesn’t say (rule 1 of [New goal](../core/rules/new-goal.md)), no metric, and the workspace called “Platform Engineering”. The reviews a goal joins read each review’s `scope` in workspace.json. `rows` is each row as `label: sentence`, separated by ` | `; `after` the “After you publish” lines, separated by ` | `.

- **metrics.csv**: The metric library’s rules ([the library as a place](../modules/metrics/rules.md)), not part of stage 1, scored like find.csv when asked (`"also": ["metrics"]`). Made on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (the same `asOf`), with the metric records under `modules.metrics` in workspace.json (`metrics` and `metricLinks`); a link counts while its goal is live then. Kinds of row, by `rule`: **find** (rule 1), one per search in a fixed list, `ask` the search as `key=value` joined by `&` (`q`, `unit`, `teamId`, `ownerId`, `dir`, `unused`, `sortout`, `retired`, `stage`, `toVerify`, `sort`; empty for nothing asked), `total` how many match and `ids` every metric id found in order (every page); **goals** (rule 2), for each metric in use by id, a head row (`row` 0: `total` its goals, `summary` the lowest-and-highest line or empty), then one row per goal in order (`row` 1, 2…): `goal` its key, `status` its code, `slice`, `now`, `target`, `vs_plan` and `owner` in words; **needs** (rule 3), for each metric, `needs` the codes in order separated by spaces, empty for none; **still** (rule 6, [defining a metric well](../modules/metrics/rules.md)), for each metric, `still` its line in words (“Fully defined”, or “Still to say: …”); **parts** (rule 7, [for, which part](../modules/metrics/rules.md)), for each metric, `parts` the parts its links in force use, most used first, each in its most used spelling, separated by “ | ”, empty for none. **ends** (rule 10), for each metric, `retire` or `delete`; **reading** ([a reading in a check-in](../modules/metrics/rules.md), NR rule 1), for each goal in force measured by a metric the demo’s number sources read, in goal id order (`row` 1, 2…): `goal` its key, `slice` its team id or `company`, then “ · {part}”, `reading` what the source says for that slice at the moment (“{value} at {ISO time}”, `none`, or `no-slice` when it reads the metric but not that slice) and `state` rule 1’s state with nothing typed, against the goal’s latest check-in by `postedAt`. The demo’s sources are seeded series made from workspace.json’s check-ins (`src/modules/metrics/numbers.ts`, `DEMO_SERIES`): for each slice, the latest check-in value of each week of the goal named, continued one week by the mean step of its last four numbers rounded to whole numbers, plus `add`, less `short` weeks at the end, each measured at 09:00 UTC on its week’s review day. **stage** ([metric quality](../modules/metrics/rules.md), MQ2), for each metric, `stage` (`draft`, `defined` or `verified`) at the moment and `missing` the parts it still needs for Defined, in order, separated by spaces (`meaning`, `calculation`, `scope`, `unit`, `direction`, `window`, `source`, `sourceOwner`, `refresh`, `owner`). A **goals** row’s `slice` is the team or “The whole company”, then “ · {part}” when the link is for one part. Every other column is empty.

- **reviews.csv**: Reviews’ rules for its switch ([Reviews](../modules/reviews/README.md)), not part of stage 1, scored when asked (`"also": ["reviews"]`). Made on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (the same `asOf`). Two kinds of row, by `rule`: **due** (rule RS1, one phrase for the clock), for each week from 1 to the week of `builtFor`, a row with Reviews `on` and one `off`: `held` is `yes` when a review is held on the week’s due day (its weekday is the cycle’s due day and the week is one of its sessions: a multiple of its `everyWeeks`), and `by`, `after`, `on_time` and `flag` are dueWords’ words (“before Thursday’s review” only with Reviews on and a review held that day, else “by Thursday”; the flag “Due by Thu 5 Nov.” either way); **readback** (rule RS2), one row: `risks` the risks a review accepted on goals not removed (notes, not removed, whose words start “We accept the risk: ”) and `due_day` the due day’s name. Every other column is empty.

- **tags.csv**: Fields’ rule ([Fields](../modules/tags/README.md), rule tags-fields), not part of stage 1, scored when asked (`"also": ["tags"]`). The demo has no field, so the rows are the rule’s cases on two fields: Stage, a list of Discover, Build and Run, and Programme, free text. Two kinds of row, by `rule`: **value**, a goal’s value as `typed` for `field`, and what it is `kept` as (empty: cleared) or the `problem` that refuses it; **field**, a field named `field` (a list’s values in `typed`, joined by |) and the `problem` that stops it being saved, empty when it saves. **filter** (rule tags-filter), Stage’s filter as a link carries it in `typed` (values joined by commas; “Not set” for no value), over four goals (g1 and g3 in Build, g2 in Discover, g4 with none), and the goals it keeps in `kept`, joined by | (a filter that picks nothing the list holds keeps every goal); **sheet** (rule tags-sheet), the question a Goals sheet’s Stage column asks about “Operate” on the rows in `case`, as `problem`, and the answers it offers in `kept` (add, empty), an admin’s or not. Every other column is empty.

- **watching.csv**: Watching’s rules ([Watching](../modules/watching/README.md)), not part of stage 1, scored when asked (`"also": ["watching"]`). Made on the workspace as it stood at `builtFor` (the same `asOf`). Two kinds of row, by `rule`: **covers**, one per person who watches anything: `watches` their watches and `covers` how many goals not removed those watches cover (a goal, a goal and everything feeding it at any depth, or every goal at a level, each goal once); **readback**, one row, what switching Watching off reads back first: `people` the people with a watch, `watches` the watches, and `see_through` of those people the ones who own no goal that is not removed or stopped. Every other column is empty.

- **home.csv** ([Home](../core/rules/home.md)): stage 3’s, scored like find.csv (`"also": ["home"]`). For four viewers (`tunde` owns two goals, `rhea` owns goals and is in a review, `amara` owns none and leads reviews, `oskar` only watches) on each of the fourteen days up to the moment the workspace is built for, at noon UTC (`screen-cases.json`’s `home`), in the workspace named by its `workspaceName`, with the workspace as it stood then (`asOf`) and `homeFor(homeFacts(…))`: `lead` the lead’s kind (`check-in-late`, `check-in`, `wrap-up`, `review` or `ask`: an ask waiting on the viewer, or a goal proposed for them, [Home](../core/rules/home.md)’s rule 5) and `title` its title, or both empty. The title is the lead’s large line under its eyebrow, the count (“2 check-ins to do”, “1 check-in still to do”, “6 check-ins to do before it”, “7 goals to discuss”), never the eyebrow (“Check-ins are due by …”, “{review} is today”). A review lead’s “{n} goals to discuss” counts the goals in its walk not yet marked reviewed that aren’t healthy: needing attention, or being handled; when none, “{n} with nothing flagged to mark reviewed”. `quiet` the quiet sentence and its line, joined by a space, or empty when there is a lead. The sentence is “Nothing is asked of you today.” (or the asks and proposed goals that wait) except once the week’s check-ins are all in: then the sentence is that (“Both check-ins are in for week 43.”, “Your check-in is …”, “All {n} check-ins are …”), with no “Nothing is asked of you today.” before it, and on the day they were completed the check-in’s receipt, word for word; `run` [the habit](../core/rules/habit.md)’s on-time run that day (`onTimeStreak` in the week of that day), and `forgiven` the forgiven week inside it with `late` or `missed` (`45 late`), or empty. No check-in draft is kept. Watches carry no date, so they are taken as they are now.

- **zone.csv** ([R3, time zones](../requirements/internal/r3-time-zones.md)): the home zone, scored like find.csv (`"also": ["zone"]`). Its input is `zone` in `workspace.json`, a case of its own: a home zone (`America/New_York`), a goal year starting Monday 19 October 2026, four check-ins (only `postedAt` matters) posted near midnight there and either side of the night the clocks go back (Sunday 1 November, 02:00 back to 01:00), and the moments to judge them at. One row per moment and goal, by moment then goal: `home_time` is the home zone’s clock (`yyyy-mm-dd hh:mm`); `week` is the goal year’s week, counted in the home zone (it turns at midnight on Sunday there, not in UTC); `latest_posted` is the goal’s check-in posted most recently by the moment (empty: none); `days_without_update` counts calendar days between the two in the home zone; `stale` is `yes` at 14 or more. The reference is `src/spec/zones.ts`: read both moments on the home zone’s wall clock and count as the UTC rules do. The rest of the workspace is judged in UTC, as before: a home zone of UTC changes nothing.

Numbers are written with up to 6 decimal places and no trailing zeros; text with commas or quotes is quoted as CSV does. Every yes-or-no column (`greener`, `needs_attention`, `forecast_misses`, `asks_target`, `needs_path`) is written `yes` or `no`; a list of codes (`flags`, `missing`, `call_missing`) is separated by single spaces and empty when there are none.

## The core alone (core-only/)

The rows above are made with every feature module on, as Faro is installed (Reviews holds sessions, Feedback has its menu row, Watching and the Wrap-up lead Home). The core must work without any module, so stage 3 has a second set: `core-only/workspace.json` is the same workspace with `modulesOff` naming every module (`navigation.csv`, `readback.csv`, `find.csv`, `home.csv` made from it, with the same `screen-cases.json`). A core rebuilt without any module scores against it with `--expected spec/conformance/core-only`; a rebuild that reads `modulesOff` passes both. Each rule takes whether a module is on as an input (the menu without Reviews or Feedback, Home with no review lead, the read-back joining no review); the screens still show a switched-off module’s address as Page not found ([the module platform](../rebuild/module-platform.md)). navigation.csv’s rows don’t score that: its `page` is the name the naming rule gives an address (`pageName`), which doesn’t read whether a module is on, so here too the rows at a module’s addresses (Watching’s `/watching`, Reviews’ `/reviews/weekly` and `?review=weekly`, the Wrap-up’s `/retro`, the example module’s `/example`, for each viewer) give the name its page has with the module on.

**module-files.json** lists each feature module’s own file above (reviews.csv, tags.csv, watching.csv…) with its key columns; the harness reads it, so a module’s file is scored when `drill.json` names it under `"also"` or `--files` does. **module-cases.json** holds, by file, the inputs of the cases a module file’s rows don’t carry themselves (metrics.csv’s searches and Metrics sheet rows, tags.csv’s fields, values, filters and questions); the harness copies it beside `workspace.json`, as it does `change-cases.json`. Read the cases from there, never from the expected files.

## The edge-case workspace (edge/)

The demo exercises most rules on most days, but not all: the full drill’s first stage 1 rebuild guessed three rules wrong and still scored 100%, because the demo has no range kept between two bounds, no ties in posting time and no correction that should or shouldn’t stop a moment. [edge/workspace.json](edge/workspace.json) is a second, small workspace of those cases (18 goals, 81 check-ins, a 13-week goal year starting 2026-01-05, built for 2026-04-02T12:00:00.000Z, week 12), with the same fields, read the same way. Its records are inputs written by hand (`src/spec/edge.ts`); every row in the files beside it is made from them by the same code as the demo’s. Only stage 1’s files are made from it: [status.csv](edge/status.csv) (224 rows), [flags.csv](edge/flags.csv) (224 rows), [projection.csv](edge/projection.csv) (224 rows), [scorecard.csv](edge/scorecard.csv) (890 rows), [checkin.csv](edge/checkin.csv) (81 rows), and [scorecard-words.csv](edge/scorecard-words.csv) when asked. The drill runs the rebuild on it as well, whenever one of those files is scored, and fails a rebuild that misses a row there as it does on the demo. It has `"edge": true`, which only says so: a rebuild reads it like any other workspace, and needn’t write the other files from it.

| Goal | Its case (and the drill gap it closes) |
|---|---|
| E-1 Availability kept between two bounds | A range kept between 99.5 and 99.95 (margin 0.1): inside, near each bound, at each bound, past each bound, and back (1.8). |
| E-2 Change failure rate at most 12% | At most 12 (margin 2): at the margin’s edge, inside it, at the limit and just past it (1.8). |
| E-3 Test coverage at least 80% | At least 80 (margin 5): the same from below, and two numbers for one week, the later posted the same day (1.14). |
| E-4 Signups who finish set-up | A share planned from 30 to 75%: 110 and 400 are both refused as over 100% (1.9). |
| E-5 Growth on last year | Planned from 50 to 150%, so not a share: 120 is only questioned; −5% is refused (1.7, 1.9). |
| E-6 Services with a runbook | The target met in week 2, nothing for week 3, met again in week 4: the week before is week 2, so no moment; met again in week 7 after falling short (1.3). |
| E-7 Alerts with an owner | Corrections: a second check-in for week 2 (no moment); week 5 posted before week 4, which then reaches the target (a moment); a late week; a backfilled week (no moment) (1.3). |
| E-8 Deploys a day | Behind in weeks 2, 3 and 5 with nothing for week 4, then on track: back 4; behind for one week: nothing (1.2). |
| E-9 Builds under ten minutes | Two check-ins for one week posted at the same moment, twice, in each record order: the status keeps the first record, the calculation the last (1.12). |
| E-10 Hours of on-call each week | Weeks 4 and 5 posted at the same moment: the status keeps week 4’s, the calculation week 5’s (1.12); later a time unit below zero, refused (1.7). |
| E-11 Cost per build | Added in week 3 with a plan from week 5: nothing due before it (1.6); money below zero, refused (1.7). |
| E-12 Pages answered in five minutes | Off track with a path back by week 5 and an action agreed after: in hand, then needing attention again once the path’s week passes (1.5). |
| E-13 Legacy jobs moved | Stopped in week 6: in every file up to week 5, then gone. |
| E-14 Cache warm-up time | Milliseconds below zero: not a time unit for that rule, so not refused (1.7). |
| E-15 Customer effort score | Held to no number: no status from its plan and nothing due, even with a check-in (1.6). |
| E-16 Runbooks tested this quarter | A check-in with no number after three with one: its calculation is none, yet it still projects from the earlier weeks’ numbers (stage 1 gap 16). |
| E-17 Teams on the new pager | A stepped plan (its first step in week 5): before it, a number moved the right way is on track, not well ahead, and one moved the wrong way is at risk, behind (stage 1 gap 6). |
| E-18 Deploys a week per team | Guarded by E-2: on plan itself, but at risk at the check-in in week 5, when E-2 is just past its limit; the status’s own calculation ignores the guard (stage 1 gap 17). |

## How a rebuild proves itself

1. Read `workspace.json`.
2. For each week from 0 to the week it was built for, take the workspace as it stood at that week’s moment (above), and for each goal there, in key order, compute the status, flags, projection and scorecard with the rebuilt rules; and for each check-in in the workspace, what a check-in must say.
3. Write the five files with the same columns and compare them row by row with these. Every difference is a rule that differs: the first few rows that differ, for one goal, usually name it.
4. Do the same with `edge/workspace.json`, and compare with the files in `edge/`.

A rebuild of the status rules alone can compare `status.csv` first, then the projection, then the flags (which need the trend and asks), then the scorecard.

Regenerate with `npm run spec` after changing a rule or the demo workspace, and commit the files it writes.
